title: Endpoint Composition PRD and Launch Readiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Product requirements for a modular, composable hosted endpoint surface that exposes chat, completions, embeddings, and reranking as first-class operations while enabling shared routing, consistent auth, and predictable SLAs. This PRD focuses on API contracts, acceptance criteria, testing strategy, and an actionable launch readiness checklist for GA of the composed endpoint surface.
goals: Provide a single, predictable hosted inference surface that supports chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank with consistent auth and billing
Ensure backward compatibility with current hosted endpoint customers and SDKs
Deliver clear operational guardrails (SLOs, throttles, fallbacks) and observability for per-route cost/latency
Support staged rollout with canary, regional opt-ins, and auto-fallback to compatible model variants
background: Multiple teams use disparate endpoint shapes for text generation, chat, embeddings, and rerank. This fragmentation increased developer friction, led to inconsistent observability and billing granularity, and complicated routing/fallback policies. The platform-level goal is to harmonize the surface while preserving low-latency and cost optimizations (batching, KV cache).
scope_included: API surface definitions for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank with unified authentication and rate limiting
Compatibility layer in SDKs (Node, Python) and REST contracts
Runtime routing rules: latency-first, cost-first, and tiered fallbacks
Observability dashboards for per-operation latency, token cost, error rate
Launch checklist and staged rollout plan including canary and regional gating
scope_excluded: New model training or model catalog additions (out of scope for this launch)
Major console redesign unrelated to endpoint-specific dashboards
Dedicated hardware procurement for enterprise customers (handled by Dedicated roadmap)
requirements: REQ-001: Expose four operations: chat.create, completions.create, embeddings.create, rerank.create with documented request/response schemas
REQ-002: Support streaming responses for chat and completions with chunked event frames and reconnection semantics
REQ-003: Preserve existing per-token billing semantics and expose token breakdowns per operation in usage API
REQ-004: Offer an opt-in compatibility flag to preserve legacy endpoint behavior for 6 months
REQ-005: Enforce tenant-level rate limits and quotas configurable via Console and API
REQ-006: Instrument per-request traces and token cost labels for Console and logs
REQ-007: Provide deterministic acceptance criteria and regression tests as part of the CI suite
api_contract_summary: chat.create: supports messages array, function calls, streaming, and system-level instructions
completions.create: single prompt or prompt template, streaming, stop tokens, temperature/top-p params
embeddings.create: batch input of texts, deterministic vector dims, async job option for very large batches
rerank.create: accepts candidate list and query, returns ranked IDs and scores; supports top-k and thresholded filtering
acceptance_criteria: AC-01: All API operations succeed with sample compliance suite across 3 representative models (small/medium/large) in hosted environment
AC-02: Streaming semantics match spec: reconnect resumes event stream with last-event-id within 10s and no duplicate token delivery
AC-03: End-to-end 99th percentile latency for chat.create (non-streaming) <= 180ms for small models and <= 400ms for large models in default region under baseline load
AC-04: Per-route token cost breakdown available in Console and usage API within 5 minutes of request completion
AC-05: Canary rollout passes health gates for 72 hours with error rate < 0.2% and no customer-facing regressions
AC-06: SDKs (Node, Python) include updated convenience helpers and maintain backward-compatible default constructor signatures
AC-07: Security review completed and secrets/KMS integration validated for private tenants
monitoring_slos: SLO-latency: 95th percentile per-operation latency tracked hourly
SLO-error-rate: <0.5% API error rate for non-rate-limit errors
Alerting: auto-alert on degradation of token-per-second throughput or KV-cache miss spike
rollout_steps: Step 1: Internal dev-only rollout for integrated teams; smoke tests and load profiles
Step 2: Limited external canary (5% of traffic) with feature flag and telemetry verification
Step 3: Gradual ramp to 50% over 48 hours if health gates pass
Step 4: Regional expansion to EU/APAC with local routing and latency verification
Step 5: Global GA with migration guides and legacy endpoint deprecation timeline
launch_checklist: Docs: API reference, migration guide, examples for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank published
SDKs: Node and Python releases including integration tests and changelog
Billing: Token accounting validated end-to-end and billing plan mapped to new operations
Observability: Dashboards for per-operation latency, cost, and errors visible to PM and SRE
Capacity: Autoscaling policies stress-tested with 2x projected peak traffic
Security: Threat model review completed, KMS integration smoke-tested
Legal/Compliance: Data residency for EU tenants validated for hosted option
Support: Runbook and escalation path published with on-call SRE and PM contacts
Canary: 72-hour canary completed with health gates and rollback plan
Migration: Communication sent to legacy endpoint owners with deprecation timeline and opt-out flag
post_launch_tasks: Collect qualitative developer feedback via survey and 1:1 sessions
Monitor cost delta per-request and recommend Optimize profiles for high-volume customers
Ship follow-up ergonomics in Console for per-route SLA overrides
Schedule 30-day retro and incident review for any anomalies during rollout
dependencies: SRE-220: Autoscaling policy audit and tuning
SDK-88: Node and Python SDK release windows
risks: Risk: Breaking changes to existing client integrations — Mitigation: opt-in compatibility flag and 6-month support window
Risk: Latency regressions when enabling unified routing — Mitigation: pre-launch load tests and per-model kernel tuning
Risk: Cost increase for heavy-embedding customers — Mitigation: recommend quantization/Optimize profiles and provide batch job async path
notes: This PRD emphasizes a composable surface so downstream product teams can adopt per-operation semantics while relying on platform routing and cost optimizations. Expect follow-up tickets for dedicated-tenant feature parity.
